thread: Jaina's internment-camp memory of Arthas: certainty before and after the fence (kept from Sylvanas)

evidence.clue: Trigger: 'Out of the camps. He'd said it as if it explained everything.'

Memory: the year she went to Dalaran, the escort stopped within sight of an orc internment camp; Arthas dared her to crawl through wet fern to a gap under the watchtower; he whispered that she would see beasts; at the fence she saw orcs by dead fires and a female humming to an infant with its fist round her tusk. He was as sure on the way back and at the tent door. She lay awake thinking he could not see what was in front of him and never told him.

Present judgement: 'Was that fair? She'd been a child, and so had he. And the band that had fired the Garrow farm had come out of those same camps, with axes. Perhaps the fences had been the right answer all along, and she'd been unfair to a boy for years over one night in the bracken. No. He'd been sure before they reached the fence and sure crawling back from it, and today he'd been sure before she reached the end of the slips, and kind about it the whole time.'
Sylvanas does not ask why Arthas used her name; Jaina waits for the question and keeps the bracken, the fence and the female humming 'to herself'.

readerKnows: The full memory and Jaina's unresolved verdict.
povCharacterKnows: Jaina only. Sylvanas 'knows there is history' only from his using her first name before three elves and half his staff.
notes: Stays inside Jaina. The Arthas price is told at sea in Ch19 per plan.
